theory.intro: Rewrite any touching signs as a single sign, then calculate. Use a number line where helpful.
facts: Adding a positive moves **right**; subtracting a positive moves **left**.
Adding two negative integers gives a negative result: add their magnitudes and keep the minus sign.
For larger integers, split the larger magnitude to make a zero pair, as in $23-57=23-23-34=-34$.
steps: Rewrite any touching signs as a single sign.
Calculate using a number line or a mental shortcut.
On a number line, start at the first integer. Add a positive integer → move right; subtract a positive integer → move left.
For several additions and subtractions, work from left to right.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Split $57$ as $23+34$ to make a zero pair.
$\begin{aligned}23-57&=23-23-34\\&=-34\end{aligned}$

(b) Split $71$ as $46+25$ to make a zero pair.
$\begin{aligned}-46+71&=-46+46+25\\&=25\end{aligned}$

(c) Add the magnitudes and keep the minus sign.
$\begin{aligned}-38+(-17)&=-38-17\\&=-(38+17)\\&=-55\end{aligned}$

Rewrite the touching signs, then work from left to right.
$\begin{aligned}-12+(-5)-(-9)-(+7)&=-12-5+9-7\\&=-17+9-7\\&=-8-7\\&=-15\end{aligned}$
